text:
andrew: Heads-up — dashboard p99 for /v1/generate just dropped by ~300ms after the last routing policy change but client-side traces still show the same tail. dashboard shows server p99 down, client p99 unchanged. anyone see a telemetry mismatch?
jasmin: saw this too. suspecting double-instrumentation at the edge: we emit both router and proxy latencies and the rollup is using the wrong tag.
kevin: can you paste the query you're using in dashboard? last PR swapped to `route_group` rollup key.
andrew: yep, here's what the dashboard backend uses now: 
```
SELECT pctl(duration_ms, 0.99) AS p99 FROM spans WHERE service IN ("runtime","edge-router") AND tags.route_group = $route GROUP BY route_group, window(1m)
```
kevin: ah — that filters both edge and runtime spans but groups by route_group. edge-router sets `route_group` to the upstream route, runtime sets it to the model variant. they're not aligned so t-digest merge is inconsistent.
bryce: so when we merge t-digests across different tag semantics we can get quantile inversion. that would explain server p99 going down (edge dists dominated by fast cached replies) while client still sees runtime tail.
jasmin: proposed fix: restrict the query to `service = "runtime"` for the server-side pctl panel, and create a separate panel for edge-proxy p50/p95/p99. also add a badge that shows sampling source.
kevin: agreed. also we should surface sample counts. currently panels display only p50/p95/p99; ops keep asking "is this real or low sample noise?". add `count()` and `sum(sample_weight)` in hover.
andrew: another wrinkle: routing quota fallback path injects a 503->retry path which is instrumented at the client and looks like a long tail. some clients retry aggressively, making client p99 worse even though server p99 for successful requests drops.
sre-oncall: @andrew what timeframe did this start? any correlating deploys?
andrew: started ~1735000800, routing-policy rollouts: `route-weight` -> `route-policy-v2` at 1735000700. deploy-bot: rollout health: 100% success.
deploy-bot: rollout `route-policy-v2` completed. no errors above threshold.
kevin: ok plan: 1) adjust dashboard queries to separate `service` and `instrumentation_source` tags, 2) show sample_count, 3) annotate the chart with rollout id, 4) add a tooltip explaining when pctl is from merged t-digests vs single-source.
bryce: for long term, we should change the rollup contract: t-digest keys must include `instrumentation_source` and `route_group` semantically aligned. otherwise merges are unreliable.
jasmin: UX note for console: when a rollout is active, show a lane that says "percentiles may be unreliable while routes are merging" + link to docs. less yelling in #eng when lights look weird. :sweat_smile:
andrew: putting a short PR to update the p99/runtime panel now. will add sample_count hover.
kevin: also add a debug panel that computes percentiles from raw histograms for troubled endpoints (fallback) so SRE can validate t-digest merge effect.
sre-oncall: i'm adding an alert that fires when p99 drops >150ms but sample_count < 50 in last 5m. low-sample flaps are noisy.
andrew: thanks — will post a screenshot when patch lands.
jasmin: small gotcha: our metrics exporter currently normalizes duration to microseconds in one path and ms in another. make sure unit normalization happens before t-digest ingestion.
bryce: ugh. add an ingestion validation that rejects spans without `duration_unit`. file ticket?
andrew: filed https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821 — put it in this sprint.
kevin: cool. one more ask: for rollouts, include the active route weights in the dashboard annotation so we can correlate percentiles with weight shifts.
jason: (reaction) :thumbsup:
kevin: wrapping up: will open PRs for panels, annotator, and alert. will coordinate with ops for a quick verification after deploy.
deploy-bot: PR #8241 merged to staging.
andrew: deployed to staging. staging panel shows server p99 stable and client p99 still high — confirms routing fallback + client retries. good catch.
jasmin: nice. leaving a note in the rollout playbook to check `instrumentation_source` alignment before major routing changes.
andrew: closing the thread once changes are in prod. thanks all.
